items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code itself is clear, but the new check `raise ValueError("Cannot filter a query once a slice has been taken.")` in Prefetch.__init__ is misleading: no filtering happens there. The docs also gained a stray double blank line.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Small, contained change. But the guard went into Prefetch.__init__ instead of a shared helper in related_descriptors.py, and it fixes the 'cannot slice' limitation in place. That error text already exists as a TypeError in filter(), so the same message now exists under two exception types.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It validates input at the boundary, but it rejects valid use instead of supporting it. It also reuses filter()'s guard message under a different exception type (ValueError vs the existing TypeError), so callers can't catch both the same way. No errors are swallowed.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: No per-parent slicing at all. Sliced querysets are rejected with `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError(...)` instead of being handled with Window/RowNumber. All 4 F2P PrefetchLimitTests fail (0/4).
